sentences.text: This creature possessed eleven teeth in the upper jaw that extended further back than in its relatives.
The specific name honors Li Xiumei, the fossil's donor.
The animal is known from a single, crushed holotype skeleton found in the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning Province.
The species Fenghuangopterus lii was described and named in 2010 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.

Fenghuangopterus belongs to the subfamily Scaphognathinae, which was previously known only from the Late Jurassic. It is a Rhamphorhynchid of this subfamily, which includes the genera Scaphognathus, Sordes, and Harpactognathus.
The animal lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Kimmeridgian stages.
